title: The Tang Pilgrim Party
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: Four sworn travellers on a commissioned journey whose one rule is that the road goes west and nothing may turn it aside.
standalone_fallback: Use the party as a small sanctioned expedition (a leader, a fighter, a muscle-and-appetite companion, a quiet guard) that must cross one impassable barrier before the story can move on.

reach.why: Heaven, Buddha and a dozen lesser powers act to protect the journey.

force.why: Wukong matches the Bull King for over a hundred rounds twice.

wealth.why: They live on alms and hospitality and bribe no one.

secrecy.why: They arrive announcing their commission at every door.

symbols: Palm-Leaf Fan carried on a shoulder
doctrine_taboos: Never turn away from the West
Wukong's kinship bonds restrain him from killing kin

sections.heading: Philosophy & Goals
sections.text: Reach the scriptures. The party answers to a Buddhist decree, not to local lords, and the master will not take another road.

sections.heading: Structure & Ranks
sections.text: Tripitaka decides; Wukong acts; Eight Rules complains and then fights; Sha Monk guards the luggage and the master.

sections.heading: Methods & Resources
sections.text: Disguise, negotiation by kinship, brute force, and appeal to Heaven when force fails.

sections.heading: Allies and Rivals
sections.text: Allied with Lingji and the Heavenly host; hostile to the Bull King's two households; welcome but dependent among the villagers.

sections.heading: Internal Tensions
sections.text: Eight Rules wants another road; Wukong's old bonds make him spare enemies the others would kill; Tripitaka's fear of the fire is hidden behind duty.

sections.heading: Joining and Dealing With Them
sections.text: Outsiders cannot join. They can feed them, guide them or bind them with debt; the party always repays.

sections.heading: Using them in play
sections.text: Run them as the PCs' travelling companions or as a patron that arrives, solves one problem violently, and leaves the aftermath to the local power.

title: The Households of the Mountain of Flames
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
provides: Lore: Local Knowledge of the Barrier
summary: Red-roofed farming villages that cannot grow a grain without a distant keeper's rain and who have no ruler but a banished spirit.
standalone_fallback: Use the households as any farming community whose harvest depends on a ritual tribute to a powerful outsider and who will pay a stranger to break the dependency.

reach.why: A string of villages near one mountain; the householder knows only the next stage of the road.

force.why: No guards or fighters appear; the local spirit's ghost soldiers are Heaven's, not theirs.

wealth.why: Nothing grows without the fan; they offer pigs and sheep once a decade.

secrecy.why: Everything about them is public: red roofs, public rituals.

doctrine_taboos: Never approach the keeper without gifts

sections.heading: Philosophy & Goals
sections.text: Keep the fan's rain and the fire at bay; every season is hot, and every harvest is borrowed.

sections.heading: Structure & Ranks
sections.text: A householder speaks for the village; no ruler; the mountain's spirit is the only official.

sections.heading: Methods & Resources
sections.text: Pilgrimage with four hogs, four sheep, flowers, fruit, fowl and wine, once every ten years; a month's round trip.

sections.heading: Allies and Rivals
sections.text: Friendly to the pilgrims; neutral toward the fan's keeper, whom they know only by a title.

sections.heading: Internal Tensions
sections.text: Some say the fire returns each year, others each decade; the party's arrival makes the households ask if the monks caused the fire.

sections.heading: Joining and Dealing With Them
sections.text: Offer a gift, bathe, and ask the householder. Outsiders become hosts or guests for a night.

sections.heading: Using them in play
sections.text: A safe, rumour-rich start; an NPC well for local knowledge; their harvest clock raises pressure whenever the fire returns.

title: The Palm-Leaf Cave Household
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
requires: Lore: News of a Lost Son
summary: A strict cultivators' cave with a single treasure that can end a region's drought or send an army across a continent.
standalone_fallback: Use the household as an isolated sorceress with a world-altering tool, an old grudge and a husband who left her; she negotiates only from strength.

reach.why: Her fan controls fire, wind and rain over an eight-hundred-li region and can blow a person 84,000 li.

force.why: Swords and the fan; she loses a wrestling bout with Wukong's rod and a stomach assault.

wealth.why: A decade of village tribute and the Bull King's sent jewels, silk and rice.

secrecy.why: Known only by a title; the fan's formulae are oral secrets.

doctrine_taboos: A treasure is not lent lightly

sections.heading: Philosophy & Goals
sections.text: Hold her cultivation and her fan; avenge Red Boy; keep a husband who is rarely home.

sections.heading: Structure & Ranks
sections.text: Rakshasi, her maids and her gate attendant. No male inside.

sections.heading: Methods & Resources
sections.text: The fan, two swords, wine and a good memory for grievances.

sections.heading: Allies and Rivals
sections.text: The Bull King's first wife and rival of Jade Countenance; hostile to Wukong.

sections.heading: Internal Tensions
sections.text: She wants her son and her husband, but cannot hold both; drink loosens her tongue and her secrets.

sections.heading: Joining and Dealing With Them
sections.text: Approach with Red Boy's news or the Bull King's name; offer, do not demand.

sections.heading: Using them in play
sections.text: A diplomacy-and-duel hub with a loot-and-secret ending, and a good source of reversals.

title: The Hoard-Thunder Court
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: A household bought with a fox king's fortune, defended by a hundred beast-spirits, and run by a demon king who splits his time between two wives.
standalone_fallback: Use the court as a wealthy bandit-lord's seat whose strength depends on one man's reputation and whose weakness is a divided home.

reach.why: The Bull King has friends at the lagoon and a name known across the West.

force.why: A hundred-plus guards plus a demon king who ties the Great Sage.

wealth.why: A ten-thousand-year fox king's fortune given as dowry.

secrecy.why: Wukong finds the cave from a single question to its mistress.

doctrine_taboos: Never slight a friend's wife or concubine

sections.heading: Philosophy & Goals
sections.text: Keep the fortune and the husband; enjoy the library and the banquets; take revenge for the son.

sections.heading: Structure & Ranks
sections.text: The Bull King commands; Jade Countenance holds the purse; a captain runs the outer guard.

sections.heading: Methods & Resources
sections.text: Wealth, a beast garrison, shape-changing and friends with other courts.

sections.heading: Allies and Rivals
sections.text: Allied with the lagoon dragons; at odds with Rakshasi's household; hunted by Heaven.

sections.heading: Internal Tensions
sections.text: The first wife's claim, the second wife's money and a husband who leaves one to please the other.

sections.heading: Joining and Dealing With Them
sections.text: Flattery and gossip about his wives are the quickest keys; he is slow to forgive insults to either.

sections.heading: Using them in play
sections.text: A moral-complication stronghold: a siege that can end in a trial of loyalties rather than just a fight.

title: The Green Wave Lagoon Court
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: An aquatic court whose politics is the banquet and whose security is its etiquette.
standalone_fallback: Use the court as a neutral hall where rival lords meet to drink; entering in disguise costs only a poem, being unmasked costs the host his dignity.

reach.why: Hosts the Bull King and attendants from across the region.

force.why: Dragon sons seize intruders, but flog rather than kill.

wealth.why: Gold roof tiles, jade frames, coral railings, pearl light.

secrecy.why: Its hall is a stage for being seen.

doctrine_taboos: The sentence for a breach is flogging

sections.heading: Philosophy & Goals
sections.text: Host; be seen; avoid quarrels that reach the hall.

sections.heading: Structure & Ranks
sections.text: The old dragon rules; sons and grandsons enforce; courtiers intercede.

sections.heading: Methods & Resources
sections.text: Banquets, music and a water-repelling gate that keeps a dry floor.

sections.heading: Allies and Rivals
sections.text: Friend to the Bull King; wary of the Great Sage once he is recognised.

sections.heading: Internal Tensions
sections.text: Courtiers will plead for a ridiculous intruder to avoid a scene.

sections.heading: Joining and Dealing With Them
sections.text: Arrive by invitation or in humble disguise; speak in verse.

sections.heading: Using them in play
sections.text: An infiltration set-piece where the prize is a mount, a rumour or a good enemy.

title: The Heavenly and Buddhist Enforcement Host
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
requires: Lore: Knowledge of the Offender's True Form
summary: A chain-of-command army that moves only on a decree and, once it moves, closes every quarter of the sky.
standalone_fallback: Use the host as a distant imperial enforcement arm that intervenes only after a formal petition and always arrives in overwhelming strength.

reach.why: Guardians at four mountains and a general in the sky.

force.why: They seal the Bull King's every escape and reduce him to a roped bull.

wealth.why: Treasure mountains and heavenly weapons, but no coin appears.

secrecy.why: Acts by secret command of Tathagata and the Jade Emperor's decree.

doctrine_taboos: No god may withhold protection from the scripture journey

sections.heading: Philosophy & Goals
sections.text: Defend the journey and the decree; arrest the Bull King and lead him to the Buddha.

sections.heading: Structure & Ranks
sections.text: A devaraja commands; a prince executes; four guardians hold the quarters.

sections.heading: Methods & Resources
sections.text: Nets, a mirror, a fiery wheel, a rope and a sword that cannot kill a head that regrows.

sections.heading: Allies and Rivals
sections.text: Allied with the pilgrims and Little Sumeru; hostile to the Bull King.

sections.heading: Internal Tensions
sections.text: Nata's methods outpace his father's patience; the guardians wait for a command.

sections.heading: Joining and Dealing With Them
sections.text: Only via petition: a memorial goes up, a decree comes down, the host arrives.

sections.heading: Using them in play
sections.text: A deus ex machina with a cost: the PCs' stand-down is the price of their intervention.

title: The Little Sumeru Temple
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
provides: Lore: Counter to a Wind Artifact
summary: A single bodhisattva's mountain that holds one unused counter to the fan and gives it freely to those on the journey.
standalone_fallback: Use the temple as a one-scene boon-giver: a patient hierarch with an exact counter-item, a short audience and no time to entertain.

reach.why: Fifty thousand li from the Mountain of Flames.

force.why: Lingji's staff subdued the Yellow Wind fiend.

wealth.why: A throne and a gate worker; no treasury appears.

doctrine_taboos: Items are held for the journey

sections.heading: Philosophy & Goals
sections.text: Serve Tathagata's order by lending the right tool at the right time.

sections.heading: Structure & Ranks
sections.text: One bodhisattva and attendants.

sections.heading: Methods & Resources
sections.text: A staff and an elixir, held back until needed.

sections.heading: Allies and Rivals
sections.text: Allied with the pilgrims.

sections.heading: Internal Tensions
sections.text: Lingji's hospitality is brief by his own account; he will help, but he will not host the party or escort it back.

sections.heading: Joining and Dealing With Them
sections.text: Arrive by cloud, be announced, explain; receive and go.

sections.heading: Using them in play
sections.text: A guaranteed-boon stop that ends a failure streak and gives a sewn-in advantage with a hidden side effect.

title: The Palm-Leaf Fan: Fire, Wind and Rain
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: A supreme-yin leaf that puts out fire, raises wind or brings rain on three waves, and blows a person across the world on one.
standalone_fallback: Use as a macro-scale tool item: three waves for three effects, an enlarge-only command that must be paired with a separate shrink secret, and a hundred-wave variant for permanent effects.

potency.why: Quenches an eight-hundred-li fire in three waves; blows a mortal 84,000 li.

range.why: Rain falls on the whole burnt region only.

cost.why: No cost is stated, but the formula and the shrink secret limit use to those who learned them.

facts.cost_narrative: No stated cost; use depends on knowing both enlarge and shrink formulas.

counters.original: Fire reversed by a false fan

facts.range_note: Eighty-four thousand li drift; permanent quenching needs forty-nine waves.

sections.heading: What It Does
sections.text: Wave one: fire out. Wave two: breeze. Wave three: rain on the burnt area only. At a creature: drift of 84,000 li. Forty-nine waves end the fire for good.

sections.heading: Source & Teachers
sections.text: Born at the back of Mount Kunlun when chaos divided; its keeper shows the enlarging formula only by accident.

sections.heading: Costs & Limits
sections.text: Press the seventh red thread with the left thumb and speak the six-syllable breath formula to enlarge; the shrink formula is separate. The false fan makes fire worse.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.text: Villagers know it as the Immortal Iron-Fan's treasure; Lingji knows its origin; the Bull King knows how to shrink it.

title: The Contest of Transformations
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
requires: Lore: Knowledge of the Opponent's Counter-Forms
summary: A pursuit duel in which each shape-shifter takes the form that preys on the other's last form.
standalone_fallback: Use as a duel minigame: each round, the pursuer picks a form that beats the fugitive's last form; the fugitive escapes only by changing to something larger or by reverting.

potency.why: Both fighters have seventy-two transformations; neither wins until the gods arrive.

range.why: The contest moves across the sky and mountain.

cost.why: No stated cost beyond time and exhaustion.

facts.cost_narrative: Exhaustion over a whole day and night of fighting.

counters.original: Imp-reflecting mirror pins the creature in its true form

facts.range_note: From cave mouth to mountain skies.

sections.heading: What It Does
sections.text: Swan, vulture, eagle, phoenix, crane, deer, tiger, leopard, lion, bear, elephant, then bull and giant: each form beats or evades the last.

sections.heading: Source & Teachers
sections.text: Both fighters learned the same method; the Bull King is bulkier and slower.

sections.heading: Costs & Limits
sections.text: A caught form cannot be left once the mirror is trained on it; size matches size.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.text: The bull's last form is ten thousand feet long and eight hundred feet high; Wukong grows to a hundred thousand.

title: The Wind-Arresting Elixir
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: A single pellet that makes the swallower unmovable by a wind artifact for the rest of the arc.
standalone_fallback: Use as a one-use counter-item that nullifies the biggest wind or force effect in the scene and has an unnoticed ongoing effect.

potency.why: The fan cannot move Wukong even three times in a row.

cost.why: One pellet, one use; swallowing it is permanent.

facts.cost_narrative: Single use; swallowed unawares when Wukong becomes a mole cricket.

counters.original: Use against the palm-leaf fan only

sections.heading: What It Does
sections.text: Makes viscera firm and bones fortified; any wind from the fan fails to move the carrier.

sections.heading: Source & Teachers
sections.text: Given to Lingji by Tathagata with the Flying-Dragon Staff; never used before.

sections.heading: Costs & Limits
sections.text: A tiny silk bag; sew it under the collar to store, hold it in the mouth to use.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.text: Wukong later swallows it unknowingly; that is why the Bull King's fan fails at his first try.

title: Three Heads, Six Arms, and the Monster-Binding Kit
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: A prince's capture routine: take a many-armed war form, cut, burn, pin the shape and rope the nose.
standalone_fallback: Use as a staged capture procedure with four steps (cut, burn, mirror-pin, rope) and a clean surrender at the end.

potency.why: Takes a mountain-sized bull that Wukong cannot beat alone.

range.why: Works at melee reach and at sight range with the mirror.

cost.why: No cost stated; needs a decree and a second holder for the mirror.

sections.heading: What It Does
sections.text: Three heads and six arms; the sword beheads, the wheel burns, the mirror pins, the rope leads.

sections.heading: Source & Teachers
sections.text: A Heavenly Prince's gifts; the mirror belongs to his father.

sections.heading: Costs & Limits
sections.text: A beheaded bull regrows a head each time, so cutting alone fails.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.text: More than ten heads fall before the fiery wheel is hung on a horn.

title: The Decennial Tribute Compact
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: A farming region pays a distant keeper once a decade for rain, and nobody remembers who set the price.
standalone_fallback: Use as a village's ritual dependence on a hidden benefactor: the gift list is fixed, the benefactor never appears, and any stranger who offers a shortcut disturbs the compact.
premise: Dependence on a hidden power leads to ritual; ritual leads to resentment; resentment leads to a bargain with an outsider.

sensory.sight: Red tile, red brick, red benches, hot dust.
sensory.sound: Cart bells of the pudding peddler; chanted tribute lists.
sensory.touch: Boiling puddings; stone benches too hot to sit on.
sensory.taste: Millet cake, tea, wine for the gift.

establishment.name: The Old Householder
establishment.worldview: The compact works if everyone follows it.
establishment.leverage: He controls hospitality and local lore.
establishment.flaw: He has never seen the fan's keeper.

main_opponent.name: The Fire
main_opponent.worldview: Nothing grows here; it is natural.

tertiary_outcast.name: The Local Spirit
tertiary_outcast.worldview: The fire is his punishment and his duty.

output_dial.level_1: The compact holds; the pilgrims are a curiosity.
output_dial.level_2: The households ask the pilgrims to carry a gift to the keeper.
output_dial.level_3: The households blame the pilgrims for provoking the keeper.
output_dial.level_4: The compact breaks; the villagers march on Jade Cloud Mountain.

threat_clocks.name: The Fire's Return
threat_clocks.advances_when: A harvest month passes after a one-wave quench or the fan is withheld.

yields_resource: Authority: Ritual Compact (rain rights and the right to ask for an audience)

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: Every ten years, households bathe, load hogs, sheep, flowers, fruit, fowl and wine, and walk a month to beg an immortal for rain.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Start here: it explains the fan, the fire and the cost of both. It pairs with the Fan-Rain Grain Chain and the Fire's Return clock.

title: The Mountain of Flames
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: Eight hundred li of flame across the only road west; a bronze skull would melt.
standalone_fallback: Use as a fire-wall barrier on a road: scorching ground, no grass for miles, and a counter that must be fetched from two or three powers.
premise: A cosmic accident created the barrier; the barrier forces the journey to ask the powers it avoided.

sensory.sight: Eight hundred li of flame; red sky.

main_opponent.name: The Flames
main_opponent.worldview: Fire grows when fanned by the false.

thematic_shadow.name: Sha Monk's Dilemma
thematic_shadow.worldview: Where there are scriptures there is fire.

tertiary_outcast.name: The Local Spirit
tertiary_outcast.worldview: Serve and wait for a pardon.

output_dial.level_1: The camp is hot but safe.
output_dial.level_2: Boots scorch and the horse refuses.
output_dial.level_3: The fire climbs; the camp must retreat.
output_dial.level_4: The fire fills the road; only a god's decree opens it.

threat_clocks.name: The Mountain's Heat
threat_clocks.advances_when: The party fans with the false fan, enters unprotected or idles at camp.

yields_resource: Ecology: A passable road once the fire is quenched forty-nine times

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: A burning wall born from kicked-over brazier bricks; the fan is the only tool, the false fan makes it worse.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: The central obstacle. It links to the Fire's Return and Heat clocks and the Palm-Leaf Fan ability.

title: The Fan-Rain Grain Chain
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: One treasure sets the fire, the rain, the harvest and the pudding cart; break the chain at the top and everything downstream goes quiet.
standalone_fallback: Use as a supply chain with a single upstream owner: weather, grain, food, trade; stop the owner and everyone downstream suffers.
premise: A single owner of the key resource shapes every price and every season downstream.

sensory.sight: Green on a burnt field after rain; red roofs.

establishment.name: Rakshasi
establishment.worldview: The fan is not lent lightly.

main_opponent.name: The Bull King
main_opponent.worldview: He can shrink what he is not given.

thematic_shadow.name: Wukong with the False Fan
thematic_shadow.flaw: Forgets to ask the whole procedure.

output_dial.level_1: Rain comes yearly; the chain holds.
output_dial.level_2: Rain comes late; puddings cost double.
output_dial.level_3: One wave, one harvest, then fire again.
output_dial.level_4: Forty-nine waves; a permanent harvest but no keeper.

threat_clocks.name: The Fire's Return
threat_clocks.advances_when: A harvest month passes after the last wave.

yields_resource: Material: Rice Flour and Millet (via a quenched fire and a returned fan)

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: Fire out, breeze, rain; then sowing, reaping, flour, puddings. The villagers call it a yearly harvest; the text leaves the real cadence open.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Use it when the PCs consider keeping the fan: it shows what the region loses.

title: The Borrowed Husband
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: A demon king with two homes, two wives and one treasure that only the first wife holds; whoever impersonates him wins it.
standalone_fallback: Use as a two-household love triangle where the husband's absence is the weakness and a disguise unlocks the first wife's secret.
premise: Divided loyalty invites imitation; imitation invites betrayal; betrayal makes a lord lose more than a fan.

sensory.sight: A library of elixir books; bolts of silk and jewels sent to the first wife.
sensory.taste: Home brew from a shared cup.

establishment.name: The Bull King
establishment.flaw: Vain; sloppy about weapons and mounts.

thematic_shadow.name: Rakshasi
thematic_shadow.worldview: A wife manages; a husband provides.

tertiary_outcast.name: Jade Countenance
tertiary_outcast.worldview: She bought protection and wants it kept.

output_dial.level_1: The husband visits both wives and the gossip stays quiet.
output_dial.level_2: A false husband appears and a treasure moves.
output_dial.level_3: The real husband finds the mount gone and races home.
output_dial.level_4: One wife is dead and the other is in tears; the fan is the only thing left.

threat_clocks.name: Rakshasi's Grudge
threat_clocks.advances_when: An insult to Rakshasi, an impersonation of her husband, or a refusal to bring Red Boy.

threat_clocks.name: The Bull King's Pursuit
threat_clocks.advances_when: An hour passes with the fan outside the party's hands.

yields_resource: Climax: A true fan and a husband in pursuit

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: Wukong plays a husband, Rakshasi gets drunk, the real husband returns and changes shape to take it back.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Best placed after the first duel: the party now has a plan, the Bull King's mount and a reason to hurry.

title: The Net of Heaven and Earth
set: Journey to the West: Flaming Mountains
summary: A fugitive demon runs to each quarter and finds a guardian waiting; the sky is closed and the end is arrest.
standalone_fallback: Use as a four-corners trap: each exit is held by a named guardian; the fugitive's only alternative is surrender.
premise: The more powerful the fugitive, the more certain the net; the net needs a decree, and a decree needs a reason the gods cannot ignore.

sensory.sight: Cosmic nets spread between mountains; gold-eyed bull; fiery wheel on a horn.

output_dial.level_1: A lone guardian blocks one road.
output_dial.level_3: Four quarters are closed and the sky is blocked.
output_dial.level_4: The bull is roped and led to the Buddha; the fan is handed over.

threat_clocks.name: The Net of Heaven and Earth
threat_clocks.advances_when: A Diamond Guardian takes up a quarter.

yields_resource: Climax: A captured bull and a surrendered fan

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: North, south, east and west guardians block the Bull King; Li and Nata block the sky.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Use it to end the arc. It rewards the PCs for earlier restraint and punishes a premature ending.
